source.title: Ulster Herald, 26 April 1930, p. 5 ("Local Government Elections: Nominations in Tyrone")
source.publisher: Ulster Herald (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: nominations read on the block image of the Ulster Herald's 'Clogher Area' (26 April 1930, p. 5, article ULH19300426.2.75): 'With the exception of the possibility of a contest in the Ballygawley division ... all the nominees are returned unopposed'

note: Triennial election of the Clogher rural district councillors, 1930. Fifteen divisions were settled at the nominations (Ulster Herald, 26 April 1930, p. 5); the one possible contest, Ballygawley, ended with R. J. Campbell's withdrawal (Belfast News-Letter, 30 April 1930, p. 15). Errigal had no nominations; its retiring member, Charles M'Girr, was deemed re-elected (see the division's note). No poll was held; Tyrone's polling day was Wednesday 4 June 1930. Returned unopposed.
